subject: Vert strange bug involving mapping to size + colour and scale_area

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Vert strange bug involving mapping to size + colour and scale_area
parts:
Hi,

I've just been bitten by what seems to be a very tricky bug. I want to
map both colour and size (area) to a variable, to make the differences
a bit more apparent, and *sometimes* throws an error.

It is data-dependent: it sometimes fails with a dummy dataset, it
always fails with mine.
The environment is also influent, which is very weird: the first test
with a dummy dataset works, then mine makes it fail, then retrying
with the same dummy dataset fails. Cleaning the namespace does not
help. Quitting R does not help either. In fact, I have to close the
terminal and open a new shell, start a new R session in it and then
the dummy example works again. Very very weird...

Anyway, here is some code:


library("ggplot2")

# Try with a dummy dataset
d = data.frame(x=1:10, y=runif(10), z=runif(10))
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x,y, size=z, colour=z)) + scale_area()
# It works

# Get my data
system("curl http://dl.getdropbox.com/u/1047321/scores.csv >
scores.csv")
scores = read.csv("scores.csv")
ggplot(scores) + geom_point(aes(lon, lat, size=value, colour=value))
# OK
ggplot(scores) + geom_point(aes(lon, lat, size=value, colour=value)) +
scale_area()
# Error in data.frame(c("#404CB1FF", "#5E408BFF", "#7C3364FF",
"#9A263EFF" :
# arguments imply differing number of rows: 4, 5

# Change names, just in case
scores = rename(scores, c(lat="y", lon="x", value="foo"))
ggplot(scores) + geom_point(aes(x, y, size=foo, colour=foo)) +
scale_area()
# Error in data.frame(c("#4849A7FF", "#5B418EFF", "#6F3975FF",
"#82315CFF", :
# arguments imply differing number of rows: 6, 4

# Retry with the orignal dummy dataset
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x,y,size=z, colour=z)) + scale_area()
# Error in data.frame(c("#4D479FFF", "#683B7EFF", "#83305CFF",
"#9D253AFF" :
# arguments imply differing number of rows: 4, 7

# Clean the environment and retry
rm(list=ls())

d = data.frame(x=1:10, y=runif(10), z=runif(10))
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x,y,size=z, colour=z)) + scale_area()
# Still no luck


I hope someone can reproduce that and figure out what happens...

Thanks in advance.

JiHO

messages.subject: Re: Very strange bug involving mapping to size + colour and scale_area
parts:
Someone helped me figure out off list that the reproducibility of my
example actually depends on the random seed. So the bug is indeed data
dependent but you don't have to download my data to see it.

As for:

> The environment is also influent, which is very weird: the first
> test with a dummy dataset works, then mine makes it fail, then
> retrying with the same dummy dataset fails. Cleaning the namespace
> does not help. Quitting R does not help either. In fact, I have to
> close the terminal and open a new shell, start a new R session in it
> and then the dummy example works again. Very very weird...

this seems to be completely wrong. Indeed, today, when the plot works
with a given dataset, it always does, no matter what happens in
between. I don't know what I drank last night which made me think
otherwise...

So now I can give a minimal reproducible example:

library("ggplot2")

set.seed(1)

d = data.frame(x=1:10, y=runif(10), z=runif(10))
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x,y, size=z, colour=z)) + scale_area()

d = data.frame(x=1:10, y=runif(10), z=runif(10))
ggplot(d) + geom_point(aes(x,y, size=z, colour=z)) + scale_area()

# works

1 to 6 fail, 7, 8, 9 work, 10 fails etc.

Thank you very much to Mike Lawrence for helping me. I hope it will
help figure out the bug.

JiHO

Hmmmm, this is a rather subtle bug which I hadn't thought about before
- and I think there's problem even when the plot runs without error -
the sizes don't actually match up with the colours. The problem is
that scale_area is generating legend keys on a sqrt scale, and
scale_colour on a normal scale. Sometimes the two don't have the same
number of items (and even when they do they don't match up) creating
an incorrect legend.

You should be able to work around the bug by manually specifying the
breaks (to both scale_area and scale_colour), and I'll think about how
to fix it properly.
